result.rationale: The Healthy band is arithmetically and substantively defensible: the worst open item is only 10 days past due, and even a severe adverse news finding could not lift this buyer to Watch given the payment raw of 13.3 carries 65% of the weight. However, the score rests on an unusually thin base — the payment agent itself flags trend as "insufficient_history", with a single settled invoice on record that was paid 12 days late, so the 13.3 is closer to an absence of evidence than a demonstrated record of paying on time. Separately, the news component contributes 0.0 because no articles were matched at all, not because the buyer was screened clean; that silence is doing 35% of the work in holding the score down. The band should stand, but the underwriter should read 8.7 as low-confidence rather than low-risk, particularly given the concentration noted below.

concerns.issue: Payment score is built on almost no history. The payment review records trend as 'insufficient_history': only one settled invoice exists, and it was paid 12 days late. A 13.3 payment raw therefore reflects a lack of observed delinquency rather than an established record of prompt payment, and the one data point that does exist is a late payment.

Exposure concentration is not captured by the score. Total open exposure of approximately EUR 1.27M across 5 open invoices sits just under the single insurer's EUR 1.33M credit line, all held by one client (CL01). The formula scores probability of default (pd 0.049) and is blind to severity of loss, so near-full limit utilisation with no diversification across insurers is invisible in the 8.7.

The delinquency is live and emerging, not historical. INV000662 (EUR 236,900) is currently 10 days past due with the remaining invoices not yet due, meaning the band was set before the rest of the EUR 1.27M has been tested. A recommended action is to re-run the score as the not-yet-due invoices mature, since further slippage on a near-limit line would move the picture materially.
